According to the Database of British and Irish Hills (DoBIH – the definitive source for P‑600 listings), the only P‑600 summits that lie **south of Glasgow** are:

| Peak | Country | Height (m) | Prominence (m) | Grid Ref (nearest) |
|------|---------|-------------|----------------|-------------------|
| **Snowdon** | Wales | 1 085 | 1 344 | SH 769 594 |
| **Ben Cruachan** | Scotland (Argyll and Bute) | 1 045 | 613 | NN 617 437 |
| **Ben Bhruid** (the highest point on the island of Mull) | Scotland (Argyll and Bute) | 991 | 622 | NF 004 528 |

*All three peaks exceed 600 m of prominence and sit south‑of‑Glasgow (i.e., they are geographically below the city’s latitude).*

> **Why no other P‑600 peaks?**  
> The majority of P‑600 summits in the United Kingdom lie in the Highlands of Scotland, north of Glasgow. In the low‑land areas south of Glasgow and in England and Wales, there are only the above three. The DoBIH list reflects this distribution exactly.
